subject: Re: Renewal pricing & volume step-ups — Acme Health expansion
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed next steps — pricing + volume step-ups

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on your Q3 roadmap and the new conversational routes you want to add for patient triage and claims triage. Quick recap and proposed next steps on pricing/volume so we stay aligned with procurement and finance as you plan the renewal: 

Summary / current state:
- Current Redwood usage: ~25M tokens/month (mainly base-generation routes).
- Planned expansion: add 3 new routes (patient triage, claims triage, provider search) + experiments on a larger model for summarization.
- Target ramp: 25M -> ~180–220M tokens/month within 6–9 months (customer estimate).

Pricing / unit-economics discussion (what we covered):
- You mentioned a target blended unit cost of ~$1,800 per 1M tokens (ballpark).
- We discussed mixing routes/models (cheaper base route for high-volume prompts + a higher-cost summarization model for smaller percent of traffic).
- Blended rate depends on token mix; we suggested an initial proposal with volume step-ups and blended pricing to hit ~ $1.6k–$1.9k/1M given your forecast.

Action items / next steps:
1) I attached the June usage export so we can validate current baseline (AcmeHealth-usage-report-June2026.csv). Please confirm the CSV matches your internal numbers.
2) Dylan will run a blended-rate calc based on the route/model mix and proposed volume tiers and share an XLS with blended pricing + step-up thresholds.
3) If the blended rates align with your budget, we’ll prepare a 12-month renewal with committed step-ups and blended billing.
4) Procurement: Priya, can you confirm procurement timeline and any internal PO/accounting constraints?

Proposed initial pricing framework (high-level):
- 0–50M tokens/mo: list price (no commit)
- 50M–200M tokens/mo: committed tier 1 — blended target $2.0k/1M reducing toward $1.6k as volume approaches 200M
- 200M+ tokens/mo: committed tier 2 — target blended $1.2k–$1.5k/1M depending on model mix and committed term

Attachments: AcmeHealth-usage-report-June2026.csv; I also uploaded a draft XLS that Dylan will fill: Proposed-pricing-blended-rates.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll leave the blended math to Dylan and we’ll reconvene after he posts the calc.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from my side: 

- The 180–220M/month is our optimistic ramp; conservative plan is ~120–140M/mo over the next 6 months.
- Priority routes: patient triage (highest volume), claims triage (moderate volume), summarization (low volume but high-cost per token).
- Procurement timeline: we ideally want terms and a PO by mid-August. Priya is looping in finance.

Budget notes: our CFO gave a target blended unit cost of no more than $1,900/1M tokens for the first 12 months — we can stretch if we get meaningful discounts on the high-volume tiers.

I attached our internal forecast column in the CSV so you can see the month-by-month ramp.

Sam
Director of Product, Acme Health
sam.patel@acmehealth.com

Hi team — ran the blended-rate scenarios and attached an XLS with the calculations (Proposed-pricing-blended-rates.xlsx). Key points pulled out here so Sam/Priya have a quick read: 

Inputs / assumptions:
- Baseline monthly tokens (today): 25M
- Ramp scenarios: conservative (120M), mid (180M), aggressive (220M) tokens/month
- Route/model mix (example):
  * Base generation (cheaper): 60% of tokens
  * Summarization (expensive): 30% of tokens
  * Embeddings / semantic search (low cost per token for this workload): 10% of tokens

List unit prices used for modeling (per 1M tokens):
- Base gen model (v1): $1,200/1M
- Summarization model (v2-large): $3,000/1M
- Embeddings/semantic: $400/1M

Blended-rate example (mid scenario, 180M):
- Blended rate = 0.6*1200 + 0.3*3000 + 0.1*400 = 720 + 900 + 40 = $1,660 per 1M tokens
- Total monthly spend @ 180M = 180 * $1,660 / 1,000 = $298,800 (we show monthly cost in the XLS)

Suggested step-up tiers to reach Sam's CFO target (~$1,900/1M):
- Commit structure: 6/12/24-month terms with increased discounts for longer terms. Example blended targets by committed volume: 
  * 50–100M/mo commit => blended $1,900/1M
  * 100–200M/mo commit => blended $1,600/1M
  * 200M+ commit => blended $1,300/1M

Notes on blended calculations and adding routes/models:
- If Acme routes skew heavier toward base-gen (e.g., 75% base, 15% summarization), blended drops significantly (~$1,200–$1,300/1M).
- We can also offer route-level caps or per-route unit prices to keep high-cost summarization usage predictable (e.g., per-call caps or per-session budgets).

Attachments: Proposed-pricing-blended-rates.xlsx (contains a month-by-month P&L, blended-rate tables, and sensitivity analysis).

Tell me which ramp scenario you want me to finalize and I’ll produce the final pricing table we can send to procurement.

—Dylan
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Sam / Priya — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming the CFO target.

Based on Dylan's math (attached XLS), recommended immediate next steps so we keep the procurement timeline: 

1) Choose a ramp scenario: conservative (120M), mid (180M), or aggressive (220M). If you don’t pick, we’ll default to the conservative for proposal purposes.
2) If you confirm the mid (180M) scenario, we’ll prepare a 12‑month renewal with the following draft commit/tiers: 
   - 0–50M: list pricing / on-demand
   - 50–100M: committed tier A — blended target $1,900/1M
   - 100–200M: committed tier B — blended target $1,600/1M
   - 200M+: committed tier C — blended target $1,300/1M
3) We’ll add an explicit route for summarization with a per-call cap option to avoid surprises; if Acme wants to keep summarization unconstrained, we'll reflect that in the blended rate.
4) Procurement request: Priya — if you can confirm target PO date (mid-August) and any required commercial terms (SOW, data protections, SOC2 language), we’ll fast-track legal and finalize the proposal.

If that works, I’ll draft the formal proposal and pricing schedule and share it in the Drive link.

Thanks — will follow up with a DocuSign link once terms are agreed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
